Gonads: **testes** secrete **androgens** (**testosterone** - male characters, spermatogenesis); **ovaries** secrete **estrogen** (female characters, menstrual cycle) and **progesterone** (pregnancy maintenance). **Pineal gland** secretes **melatonin** (sleep-wake/diurnal cycle). **Thymus** secretes **thymosins** (T-lymphocyte maturation, immunity).

Hormone mechanism: **water-soluble hormones** (peptides) bind **membrane receptors** and act via **second messengers** (**cAMP**, **IP3**, **Ca2+**); **lipid-soluble** steroids/thyroxine enter cells, bind **intracellular**/**nuclear receptors** and change **gene expression**. Feedback: rising hormone levels inhibit further release (**negative feedback**, e. thyroxine inhibits TSH).

Diabetes mellitus: **insulin** deficiency causes high blood sugar (**hyperglycemia**) and glucose in urine (**glycosuria**); **diabetes insipidus** is **ADH** deficiency causing excessive dilute urine - a different disease.

Addison's disease: under-secretion of **adrenal cortex** hormones (low **cortisol**/**aldosterone**) causes bronze-like skin and weakness; **Cushing's syndrome** is the opposite - **cortisol** excess.

Non-endocrine hormone sources: **atrial natriuretic factor** (heart - lowers **blood pressure**), **erythropoietin** (kidney - stimulates **RBC formation**), **gastrin**/**secretin**/**CCK**/**GIP** (GI tract regulate digestion).

questions.q: Define the following terms: (a) exocrine gland, (b) endocrine gland, (c) hormone.
questions.a: (a) A gland with ducts that releases its secretion onto a surface or into a cavity. (b) A ductless gland releasing hormones directly into the blood. (c) A chemical messenger secreted by endocrine glands, carried by blood to target organs.

questions.q: Name the hormones secreted by the following and specify the source in each case: hypothalamus, pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, testis, ovary, thymus, atrium, kidney and gastro-intestinal tract.
questions.a: Hypothalamus: releasing and inhibiting hormones. Pituitary: GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, MSH, oxytocin, vasopressin. Thyroid: T3, T4, calcitonin. Parathyroid: parathyroid hormone. Adrenal: cortisol, aldosterone, adrenaline, noradrenaline. Pancreas: insulin, glucagon. Testis: androgens (testosterone). Ovary: estrogen, progesterone. Thymus: thymosins. Atrium: atrial natriuretic factor. Kidney: erythropoietin. GI tract: gastrin, secretin, CCK, GIP.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Hypothalamic hormones are transported to the _____ gland. (b) TSH acts on the _____. (c) ACTH acts on the _____. (d) Gonadotrophins act on the _____. (e) MSH acts on the _____.
questions.a: (a) Pituitary (b) Thyroid (c) Adrenal cortex (d) Gonads (testis/ovary) (e) Melanocytes.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched: (a) Pineal - melatonin, (b) Thyroid - tetraiodothyronine, (c) Ovary - estrogen, (d) Adrenal medulla - epinephrine, (e) all of the above?
questions.a: (e) All of the above are correct pairings.

questions.q: Write short notes on the functions of: (a) parathyroid hormone (b) thyroid hormones (c) insulin and glucagon.
questions.a: (a) PTH raises blood Ca2+ by bone resorption and renal reabsorption. (b) T3/T4 regulate basal metabolic rate, growth and development; need iodine. (c) Insulin lowers blood glucose (glycogenesis); glucagon raises it (glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis).

questions.q: Give examples of: (a) hyperglycemic and hypoglycemic hormones (b) hypercalcemic hormone (c) gonadotrophic hormones (d) blood pressure lowering hormone.
questions.a: (a) Glucagon (hyperglycemic), insulin (hypoglycemic). (b) Parathyroid hormone. (c) FSH and LH. (d) Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF).

questions.q: Which hormonal deficiency is responsible for: (a) diabetes mellitus (b) goitre (c) cretinism?
questions.a: (a) Insulin deficiency. (b) Iodine/thyroxine deficiency. (c) Thyroid hormone deficiency in infants/children.

questions.q: Briefly mention the mechanism of action of FSH.
questions.a: FSH binds membrane receptors on ovarian follicles/Sertoli cells and acts via second messengers (cAMP); in females it stimulates follicle growth and estrogen secretion, in males it supports spermatogenesis.

mcqs.q: Which of the following pairs of hormones are not antagonistic (opposing) to each other?
mcqs.why: Relaxin and inhibin are not an antagonistic pair.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is not a second messenger?
mcqs.why: cAMP, cGMP and Ca2+ are second messengers; sodium is not.

mcqs.q: Which of the following conditions is not linked to deficiency of thyroid hormone?
mcqs.why: Exophthalmia is linked to excess thyroid hormone (Graves disease).

mcqs.q: Which of the following hormones is not a secretory product of human placenta?
mcqs.why: Prolactin is secreted by the pituitary, not the placenta.

mcqs.q: Mary is about to face an interview. But during the first five minutes before the interview she experiences sweating, increased rate of heartbeat, respiration etc. Which of the following hormones are responsible for her restlessness?
mcqs.why: Adrenaline and noradrenaline (emergency hormones) cause these 'fight or flight' responses.

mcqs.q: The steroid responsible for balance of water and electrolytes in our body is:
mcqs.why: Aldosterone (mineralocorticoid) balances water and electrolytes.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities have the same dimensional formula?
dailyQuestions.why: Both work and torque have the dimensional formula M L^2 T^-2; in each other pair the dimensions differ.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: A vehicle covers half the distance with speed V1 and the remaining half with speed V2. Its average speed is:
dailyQuestions.why: For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean: 2V1V2/(V1 + V2).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: The value of the scalar product (B x A) dot A is:
dailyQuestions.why: B x A is perpendicular to both A and B, so its dot product with A is zero.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: A body of mass 2 kg moves such that its position is x(t) = pt + qt^2 + rt^3, where p = 3 m/s, q = 4 m/s^2 and r = 5 m/s^3. The force acting on the body at t = 2 s is:
dailyQuestions.why: Acceleration a = d^2x/dt^2 = 2q + 6rt = 8 + 60 = 68 m/s^2 at t = 2 s; F = ma = 2 x 68 = 136 N.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: A body is falling freely in a vacuum. Which of the following remains constant?
dailyQuestions.why: With only gravity acting and no air resistance, mechanical energy is conserved.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: Both the Earth and the Moon are subject to the gravitational force of the Sun. As observed from the Sun, the orbit of the Moon:
options: will not be strictly elliptical because the total gravitational force on it is not central
dailyQuestions.why: The Moon experiences two centres of attraction (Sun and Earth), so the net force is not central and the orbit is not strictly an ellipse.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: Streamline flow is more likely for liquids with:
dailyQuestions.why: Both low density and high viscosity keep the Reynolds number (rvd/eta) low, which favours streamline flow.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: A cubic vessel containing an ideal gas at NTP is carried by a rocket moving vertically at 500 m/s. The pressure of the gas inside, as observed from the ground:
options: increases due to the rocket's speed
dailyQuestions.why: Pressure depends on molecular motion relative to the walls, which uniform motion of the vessel does not change.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: The law of multiple proportions is illustrated by the pair:
dailyQuestions.why: CO and CO2: the same elements combine in different fixed ratios; the oxygen masses combining with a fixed mass of carbon are in the simple ratio 1:2.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: The number of radial nodes for the 3p orbital is:
dailyQuestions.why: Radial nodes = n - l - 1 = 3 - 1 - 1 = 1.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: Covalency of nitrogen is restricted to 4 but phosphorus and sulphur can expand it to 5 or 6 because of:
options: larger size of P and S
the presence of vacant d orbitals in P and S
lower electronegativity of P and S
dailyQuestions.why: Vacant d orbitals in the third period allow P and S to expand their octet.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: The molecule with the highest dipole moment is:
dailyQuestions.why: H2O has the largest net dipole (1.85 D) because of its bent geometry and the two O-H dipoles.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: The enthalpy of formation of a compound is:
dailyQuestions.why: Formation can be exothermic or endothermic; e.g. NH3 is negative but HI is positive.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: Arrange the hydrogen halides in order of decreasing reactivity with propene: (i) HCl > HBr > HI (ii) HBr > HI > HCl (iii) HI > HBr > HCl (iv) HCl > HI > HBr
dailyQuestions.why: Reactivity follows HI > HBr > HCl because the H-X bond weakens down the group, easing electrophilic addition.

dailyQuestions.subject: Mathematics
dailyQuestions.q: The complement of the union of two sets, (A union B)' is:
dailyQuestions.why: De Morgan's law: (A union B)' = A' intersection B'.

dailyQuestions.subject: Mathematics
dailyQuestions.q: The number of non-empty relations that can be defined from a set A of p elements to a set B of q elements is:
dailyQuestions.why: There are 2^(pq) relations in all; excluding the empty relation gives 2^(pq) - 1.

dailyQuestions.q: If sin theta + cosec theta = 2, then sin^2 theta + cosec^2 theta equals:
dailyQuestions.why: Squaring gives sin^2 + cosec^2 + 2 = 4, so the sum is 2.

dailyQuestions.why: Only odd powers of a survive: the terms with a^1, a^3, ..., a^51 give 26 terms.

dailyQuestions.why: Since sin x ~ x, sin^2 x - x^2 tends to 0 faster than x^2; the limit is 0.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Family names in plants end with the suffix:
dailyQuestions.why: ICBN rule: plant family names end in -aceae (e.g. Rosaceae).

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following statements is WRONG for viroids?
options: Their RNA is of high molecular weight
They cause potato spindle tuber disease
dailyQuestions.why: Viroids have RNA of low molecular weight (not high).

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following is a WRONG statement?
options: Haploid endosperm is typical of gymnosperms
Sexual reproduction in fungi may occur by conjugation
dailyQuestions.why: Mucor (zygomycete) reproduces asexually by non-motile sporangiospores - it does not produce biflagellate zoospores.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: The 'eyes' of the potato tuber are:
dailyQuestions.why: Each eye is a node bearing an axillary bud.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: A basic dye used for staining mitochondria is:
dailyQuestions.why: Janus green B specifically stains mitochondria.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: C4 plants are less limited by CO2 than C3 plants because:
options: the primary CO2 fixation is via PEP carboxylase, which has high affinity for CO2
dailyQuestions.why: PEP carboxylase has a very high affinity for CO2, so C4 plants can concentrate CO2 at RuBisCO and suppress photorespiration.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: The muscles involved in normal (quiet) breathing in humans are:
dailyQuestions.why: Quiet breathing is driven by the diaphragm and the external intercostal muscles.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
dailyQuestions.why: Blood consists of plasma plus the formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, platelets).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following pairs have the same dimensions? (Exemplar style)
options: Force and torque in every unit system differently
dailyQuestions.why: Energy and torque both have dimensions [M L^2 T^-2].

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: A car on a leveled (unbanked) circular road of radius r will skid if its speed exceeds:
dailyQuestions.why: Friction provides centripetal force: mv^2/r <= mu_s mg gives v_max = sqrt(mu_s r g).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between displacement and acceleration is:
dailyQuestions.why: a = -omega^2 x, so acceleration is opposite in phase to displacement (difference pi).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: A closed organ pipe and an open organ pipe of the same length have fundamental frequencies in the ratio:
dailyQuestions.why: Closed: v/(4L); open: v/(2L); ratio = 1:2.

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: If the temperature of an ideal gas is doubled (in kelvin) at constant volume, its pressure will:
dailyQuestions.why: P proportional to T at constant V (Gay-Lussac form of PV = nRT).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: The escape velocity from a planet of mass M and radius R is:
dailyQuestions.why: Setting (1/2)mv_e^2 = GMm/R gives v_e = sqrt(2GM/R).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: Excess pressure inside a liquid drop (one surface) of radius R is:
dailyQuestions.why: A liquid drop has a single surface, so excess pressure = 2S/R (a soap bubble, with two surfaces, is 4S/R).

dailyQuestions.subject: Physics
dailyQuestions.q: For a Carnot engine, efficiency increases when:
options: Both temperatures increase equally in Celsius reading alone
dailyQuestions.why: eta = 1 - T_cold/T_hot; raising T_hot or lowering T_cold increases eta.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: What is the number of significant figures in 0.004560?
dailyQuestions.why: Leading zeros are not significant; 4, 5, 6 and the trailing 0 are - total 4.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: The maximum number of electrons in a subshell with l = 3 is:
dailyQuestions.why: l = 3 is the f subshell with 7 orbitals, holding 14 electrons.

dailyQuestions.q: Which element has the highest first ionisation enthalpy among the following?
dailyQuestions.why: Ionisation enthalpy increases across period 3, so Si is highest here.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: The hybridisation of carbon in CO2 is:
dailyQuestions.why: CO2 is linear O=C=O with two regions of electron density: sp hybridisation.

dailyQuestions.subject: Chemistry
dailyQuestions.q: At equilibrium, the value of delta G for a reaction is:
dailyQuestions.why: At equilibrium there is no net driving force, so delta G = 0.

dailyQuestions.q: Cyclic polymerisation of ethyne through a red-hot iron tube gives:
dailyQuestions.why: Three ethyne molecules trimerise at 873 K to form benzene.

dailyQuestions.why: Gymnosperms bear naked seeds without flowers or fruits.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of events in the cell cycle?
dailyQuestions.why: Interphase follows G1, S and G2 before the M phase.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in C4 plants is:
dailyQuestions.why: PEP carboxylase fixes CO2 into oxaloacetic acid (4C) in C4 plants.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following is the universal blood donor group?
dailyQuestions.why: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigens, so they can be given to all groups.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: The functional unit of contraction in a muscle fibre is the:
dailyQuestions.why: The sarcomere, between two Z-lines, is the functional unit of contraction.

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which plant hormone is a gas and promotes fruit ripening?
dailyQuestions.why: Ethylene is the gaseous hormone that triggers fruit ripening.

dailyQuestions.q: The juxtaglomerular apparatus is formed by:
options: Loop of Henle and vasa recta
dailyQuestions.why: JGA is the cellular modification at the contact of the DCT (macula densa) with the afferent arteriole (JG cells).

dailyQuestions.subject: Biology
dailyQuestions.q: Which of the following is a reducing sugar?
dailyQuestions.why: Maltose has a free aldehyde group and reduces Fehling's solution.
